info.title: QAuth Auth Server API
info.description: OAuth 2.1 / OIDC 1.0 authorization server for MCP servers and AI agents: authorization_code + PKCE and client_credentials grants, RFC 8693 on-behalf-of agent delegation, and environment-aware authorization policy. Wallet federation (OID4VP) transport ships behind a default-off flag.

bearerAuth.description: Access token obtained from login, refresh, or OAuth token endpoint.

get.description: Apple associated domains file: the apps that share the passkeys and passwords of the realm host (`webcredentials`). Served only while the passkey RP ID is the realm host.
Digital Asset Links statement list: the Android apps that share the sign-in credentials of the realm host (`get_login_creds`). Served only while the passkey RP ID is the realm host.
Health check endpoint. Returns database and Redis connectivity status. Used for liveness and readiness probes.
Prometheus metrics endpoint. Returns process/runtime metrics plus auth counters in Prometheus text exposition format.
Root API endpoint. Returns a simple greeting to verify the auth server is running.
OAuth 2.0 Authorization Server Metadata (RFC 8414). Unauthenticated, cacheable.
OpenID Connect Discovery 1.0 document. Superset of RFC 8414 AS metadata with OIDC-specific fields. Unauthenticated, cacheable.
JSON Web Key Set (RFC 7517) containing the active EdDSA public signing key(s). Used by clients and resource servers to verify JWT signatures.

Shared Signals Framework transmitter metadata (SSF 1.0 §7): the stream management endpoints, push delivery, and the transmitter’s own JWKS (`/ssf/jwks.json`), which verifies the realm’s Security Event Tokens. 404 for a realm that does not run the transmitter.

post.description: Start linking a wallet credential to the signed-in account. Requires a valid session cookie and an `X-CSRF-Token` header matching the per-session token returned by `GET /consents`. Issues an OID4VP 1.0 presentation request in LINKING mode: the validated response is bound to the caller's authenticated users.id and is never used to resolve or create an account (ADR-009 §5). The optional `device` field (`this` | `other`, default `other`) says where the wallet is: a same-device link completes on the browser's return leg at `GET /ui/wallet-login/return` and polls as `pending` until then (OID4VP 1.0 §14.2, HAIP 1.0 §5.1); a cross-device link completes by polling. Issues #238, #405.

get.description: Poll a wallet-linking flow. Reports whether the direct_post presentation response has arrived, and COMPLETES the link when it has — writing a second user_credentials row (provider_type=wallet) under the same users.id. A link started with `device=this` completes on the return leg instead and polls as `pending` until then, then `linked` once (#405). Issue #238.

post.description: Authenticate with email and password. Returns access token, refresh token, and expiration. Requires valid credentials.

Log out the current user. Ends the user's hosted browser sessions, revokes all refresh tokens and unredeemed authorization codes for the user, and the access token presented. Accepts expired access tokens.

Register a password account. Answers every address with the same 202 and message, whether it was free or already registered; the next step arrives by email (a verification link for a new account, a notice for an existing one). Password must meet strength requirements.
Request a new verification email. Rate limited per IP and per email. Always returns success to prevent email enumeration.
Verify email address using the token sent via email, in the request body. Single-use; marks token as used. POST so no link fetch or prefetch can verify an address on its own.

get.description: List the OAuth clients owned by the authenticated developer. Scoped by oauth_clients.developer_id. Requires a developer Bearer access token. Never returns the client secret. (Phase 2.2, issue #85.)

post.description: Create an OAuth client owned by the authenticated developer. The server generates the client_id and (for confidential clients) a client_secret; the plaintext secret is returned in THIS response only and never again. Requires a developer Bearer access token. (Phase 2.2, issue #86.)

get.description: Get one of the authenticated developer's OAuth clients by id. Returns 404 if the client does not exist or is owned by another developer (no existence enumeration). Never returns the client secret. (Phase 2.2, issue #87.)

patch.description: Update mutable fields of one of the developer's OAuth clients (name, description, redirectUris, scopes, grantTypes, responseTypes, tokenEndpointAuthMethod, enabled). client_id and client_secret are immutable here. enabled is the owner's switch and may be set either way; it does not lift an operator's suspension (the read-only suspended field), which only the operator can. Returns 404 if the client does not exist or is owned by another developer. (Phase 2.2, issue #88.)

delete.description: Delete one of the developer's OAuth clients. Returns 404 if the client does not exist or is owned by another developer. After deletion the client can no longer authenticate. (Phase 2.2, issue #89.)

post.description: Issue a new client_secret for one of the developer's OAuth clients. The previous secret is invalidated immediately and the new plaintext secret is returned in THIS response only. Returns 404 if the client does not exist or is owned by another developer; 400 for a public client that has no secret. (Phase 2.2, issue #90.)

Mint a static developer API key for one of the developer's OAuth clients. ENVIRONMENT-GATED (ADR-008 §6): permitted only while the client resolves to a development environment; a staging/production (or unset-environment) client is refused with 403 and must use the OAuth client_credentials grant. The plaintext key is returned in THIS response only and never again. Returns 404 if the client does not exist or is owned by another developer. (Issue #97.)

get.description: List the static API keys for one of the developer's OAuth clients. Returns masked fields only (prefix + last4) — never the key or its hash. Includes revoked keys (with revokedAt set). Returns 404 if the client does not exist or is owned by another developer. (Issue #97.)

delete.description: Revoke one static API key for one of the developer's OAuth clients. Idempotent soft-delete: the row is retained with revokedAt set, and a revoked key never authenticates again. Returns 404 if the client or key does not exist or is owned by another developer. (Issue #97.)

get.description: List the active OAuth consents for the currently signed-in user. Drives the developer portal revocation screen (issue #150). The response also carries a per-session CSRF token that the caller MUST echo back as the `X-CSRF-Token` header on `DELETE /consents/:id`.

delete.description: Revoke an OAuth consent row owned by the currently signed-in user. Requires a valid `X-CSRF-Token` header whose value matches the session CSRF token returned by `GET /consents`.

get.description: List the active OAuth consents belonging to the authenticated user. Requires a developer Bearer access token. Drives the developer portal revocation screen (issue #366).

delete.description: Revoke one of the authenticated user's OAuth consents. Returns 404 if the consent does not exist or belongs to another user, so the API never reveals that another user's consent id exists. Requires a developer Bearer access token.

get.description: OAuth 2.1 authorization endpoint (GET). Issues an authorization code with PKCE and redirects to the client redirect_uri.

parameters.name: dpop_jkt
parameters.description: RFC 9449 §10: the base64url SHA-256 JWK thumbprint of the DPoP key to bind the authorization code to. Read only when the server has DPoP on.

post.description: OAuth 2.1 authorization endpoint (POST). Identical to GET; parameters are form-encoded in the request body (OIDC Core §3.1.2.1).

dpop_jkt.description: RFC 9449 §10: the base64url SHA-256 JWK thumbprint of the DPoP key to bind the authorization code to. Read only when the server has DPoP on.

post.description: RFC 7662 token introspection. Send access token and client credentials in application/x-www-form-urlencoded body. Returns active and claims when token is valid for the client.
OAuth 2.0 Dynamic Client Registration (RFC 7591). Open-mode — no initial_access_token required. Scope requests are capped to the realm's dynamic_registration_allowed_scopes list.
RFC 7009 token revocation. Send the token and confidential client credentials in an application/x-www-form-urlencoded body. Always returns 200 with an empty body on success.
OAuth 2.1 token endpoint. Supports authorization_code (with PKCE) and client_credentials grants. Client auth via client_secret_post or client_secret_basic.

get.description: OIDC userinfo endpoint (GET). Returns claims for the authenticated user. Requires a Bearer access token whose `aud` contains its own `client_id` or this endpoint's URL; a token for another resource server gets 401, as does a token whose subject is not a user (a client_credentials token). With DPoP on, a DPoP-bound token is accepted only under the `DPoP` scheme with a valid proof (RFC 9449 §7), and refused as a Bearer token.

post.description: OIDC userinfo endpoint (POST). Returns claims for the authenticated user. Accepts a Bearer access token in the Authorization header or a form-encoded access_token body parameter (RFC 6750 §2.2). The token's `aud` must contain its own `client_id` or this endpoint's URL; a token for another resource server gets 401, as does a token whose subject is not a user (a client_credentials token). With DPoP on, a DPoP-bound token is accepted only under the `DPoP` scheme with a valid proof (RFC 9449 §7), and refused as a Bearer token or a body parameter.

get.description: OID4VP 1.0 / RFC 9101 Request Object Endpoint. Serves the signed Authorization Request a `request_uri` refers to, as application/oauth-authz-req+jwt. TRANSPORT ONLY: the request state is neither read nor consumed here, nothing is written, and an unknown or expired reference is indistinguishable from a malformed one.

post.description: OID4VP 1.0 direct_post Response Endpoint. Accepts a wallet Authorization Response as application/x-www-form-urlencoded: in the clear (vp_token + state, or error + state) under response_mode=direct_post, or as a single `response` parameter carrying a JWE (ECDH-ES P-256, A128GCM/A256GCM) encrypted to the per-request key published in client_metadata under response_mode=direct_post.jwt. TRANSPORT ONLY: the response is correlated against a single-use presentation request and structurally parsed. No signature, credential or issuer validation is performed and no user is authenticated (that is #234/#236). Answers HTTP 200 with a JSON object (OID4VP 1.0 §8.2): `{}` for a cross-device request, or `{ redirect_uri }` for a same-device request — an absolute URI under the issuer carrying a fresh, single-use Response Code (HAIP 1.0 §5.1) that the wallet MUST redirect the user agent to.

200.description: Transport-level acknowledgement (OID4VP 1.0 §8.2): HTTP 200 with a JSON object. Confirms the response was well-formed and correlated with a pending presentation request. For a same-device request the object carries `redirect_uri` — an absolute URI under the issuer with a fresh, single-use Response Code — which the wallet MUST redirect the user agent to (HAIP 1.0 §5.1); for a cross-device request it is empty and the wallet is not required to perform any further steps. It does NOT assert that any credential was verified or that any user was authenticated.

schema.description: Transport-level acknowledgement (OID4VP 1.0 §8.2): HTTP 200 with a JSON object. Confirms the response was well-formed and correlated with a pending presentation request. For a same-device request the object carries `redirect_uri` — an absolute URI under the issuer with a fresh, single-use Response Code — which the wallet MUST redirect the user agent to (HAIP 1.0 §5.1); for a cross-device request it is empty and the wallet is not required to perform any further steps. It does NOT assert that any credential was verified or that any user was authenticated.

get.description: The JSON Web Key Set (RFC 7517) that verifies the realm’s Security Event Tokens: its active and retired `event_signing` keys. The `jwks_uri` of the transmitter metadata. Unauthenticated, cacheable for five minutes. The realm JWKS at `/.well-known/jwks.json` holds no SET key.

post.description: Create the receiver’s Shared Signals Framework stream (SSF 1.0 §8.1.1.1). Push delivery only; `endpoint_url` must be an https URL on a public address. A receiver has one stream per realm: a second create answers 409.

events_requested.description: The event type URIs the receiver wants.

endpoint_url.description: Where QAuth POSTs each SET: an `https` URL on a public address.

authorization_header.description: The `Authorization` header QAuth sends with every push. Stored encrypted and never returned.

delivery.description: How QAuth delivers the stream: push only.

description.description: The receiver’s description, cut to 1024 characters.

schema.description: A stream configuration, as a receiver sends it (SSF 1.0 §8.1.1).

requestBody.description: A stream configuration, as a receiver sends it (SSF 1.0 §8.1.1).

get.description: Read the receiver’s stream (SSF 1.0 §8.1.1.2), or, without `stream_id`, list the streams it has in this realm.

patch.description: Update the receiver-supplied members of the stream (SSF 1.0 §8.1.1.3); a member left out stays. A transmitter-supplied member may be sent only with the value QAuth holds.

events_requested.description: The event type URIs the receiver wants.

endpoint_url.description: Where QAuth POSTs each SET: an `https` URL on a public address.

authorization_header.description: The `Authorization` header QAuth sends with every push. Stored encrypted and never returned.

delivery.description: How QAuth delivers the stream: push only.

description.description: The receiver’s description, cut to 1024 characters.

schema.description: A stream configuration, as a receiver sends it (SSF 1.0 §8.1.1).

requestBody.description: A stream configuration, as a receiver sends it (SSF 1.0 §8.1.1).

put.description: Replace the receiver-supplied members of the stream (SSF 1.0 §8.1.1.4); a member left out is removed, and `delivery` is required.

events_requested.description: The event type URIs the receiver wants.

endpoint_url.description: Where QAuth POSTs each SET: an `https` URL on a public address.

authorization_header.description: The `Authorization` header QAuth sends with every push. Stored encrypted and never returned.

delivery.description: How QAuth delivers the stream: push only.

description.description: The receiver’s description, cut to 1024 characters.

schema.description: A stream configuration, as a receiver sends it (SSF 1.0 §8.1.1).

requestBody.description: A stream configuration, as a receiver sends it (SSF 1.0 §8.1.1).

delete.description: Delete the stream and its subjects (SSF 1.0 §8.1.1.5). Its deliveries still pending end without being sent.

get.description: Read the stream’s status (SSF 1.0 §8.1.2.1). `delivery_status`, QAuth’s extension, reports the deliveries still pending and the latest failed attempt from the delivery history. An endpoint QAuth refused to reach and one it could not reach both read `destination_unreachable`.

pending.description: Deliveries waiting for an attempt or a retry.

last_failure.description: The latest failed attempt of a delivery to this stream.

event_id.description: The `jti` of the SET whose delivery failed.

error.description: Why it failed, such as `http_status` or `timeout`.

delivery_status.description: QAuth’s extension: how deliveries to this stream go, from the delivery history.

post.description: Set the stream’s status (SSF 1.0 §8.1.2.2): `enabled`, `paused` (events are held, however long, without spending attempts, and sent within 30 seconds of it being enabled again) or `disabled` (nothing is held).

pending.description: Deliveries waiting for an attempt or a retry.

last_failure.description: The latest failed attempt of a delivery to this stream.

event_id.description: The `jti` of the SET whose delivery failed.

error.description: Why it failed, such as `http_status` or `timeout`.

delivery_status.description: QAuth’s extension: how deliveries to this stream go, from the delivery history.

post.description: Add a subject to the stream (SSF 1.0 §8.1.3.2). The transmitter’s `default_subjects` is `NONE`: the stream receives events only about the subjects added. A user is named `iss_sub` with the realm’s issuer, a client `uri` or `opaque` by its `client_id`; another subject is kept and matches no event.
Remove a subject from the stream (SSF 1.0 §8.1.3.3). A subject the stream does not have answers 204 as well.

Ask for a verification event on the stream (SSF 1.0 §8.1.4.2). QAuth records the request as an event and pushes the verification Security Event Token to this stream only, with `state` returned as sent. A second request within `min_verification_interval` (10 seconds) answers 429.

get.description: Render the OAuth consent screen. Requires a valid __Host-qauth_session cookie; otherwise redirects to /ui/login.

parameters.name: dpop_jkt
parameters.description: RFC 9449 §10: the base64url SHA-256 JWK thumbprint of the DPoP key to bind the authorization code to. Read only when the server has DPoP on.

post.description: Submit the consent decision. CSRF-protected; re-uses the authorize params to issue a code on Allow.

dpop_jkt.description: RFC 9449 §10: the base64url SHA-256 JWK thumbprint of the DPoP key to bind the authorization code to. Read only when the server has DPoP on.

get.description: Renders the session-cookie login page. `return_to` is a relative path to redirect to after a successful sign-in. Issue #150.

post.description: Submit the session-cookie login form. Sets __Host-qauth_session on success.

get.description: Resume a pending authorization request after login. The handle is single-use and resolves ONLY to an authorize URL this server minted. Issue #316.
Renders the wallet-linking confirmation screen for the signed-in user. Issue #238.

post.description: Starts a wallet-linking flow for the signed-in user and issues an OID4VP presentation request. Issue #238.

get.description: Re-renders a wallet-linking flow in progress, completing it if the wallet has responded. Also the no-JavaScript refresh path. Issue #238.
Renders the wallet sign-in screen, which collects the account identifier the user asserts (ADR-009). Issue #239.

post.description: Starts a wallet sign-in: records the asserted account identifier and issues an OID4VP presentation request. Issue #239.

get.description: Re-renders a wallet sign-in in progress, advancing it if the wallet has responded. Also the no-JavaScript refresh path. Issue #239.
Polled by the wallet sign-in screen. Reports whether the direct_post presentation response has arrived, and completes the sign-in when it has. Issue #239.

Same-device return leg of a wallet sign-in (OID4VP 1.0 §8.2 / §14.2, HAIP 1.0 §5.1). The wallet redirects the browser here with the single-use Response Code (43 base64url characters) it received from the direct_post Response Endpoint; the code is spent first, then matched against the flows this browser holds, and the sign-in completes only in the browser that started it. Every refusal renders one identical page. Issue #405.
